YOUR GET-STARTED CHECKLIST
            BE READY IN 30 DAYS

  BUILD YOUR READING AND LISTENING HABITS
  You want to build your reading speed, vocabulary and grammar, as well
  as ideas for the writing and speaking tasks. Read newspapers and
  listen to podcasts or news radio.

  LEARN THE TASKS AND E2 METHODS
  Understand the test and the best methods to improve your performance.
  You can do it alone, but it will be faster with a teacher.

  PRACTICE
  Start reading, writing, speaking and listening. Get comfortable with the
  test. Practice, repeat and internalise what you've learned in class.
  Check the answers carefully.


  TAKE THE E2 MOCK TEST
  Take a simulation test; see your improvement; see where improvement is
  still needed. Get detailed feedback and find out what you need to work
  on.


  KNOW YOUR STRENGTHS AND WEAKNESSES
  Do you need better vocabulary? More reading? Grammar accuracy?
  Where do you need to spend more time? Find out what you need to do
  next, prioritise, and execute.


  TALK TO AN E2 EXPERT
  Book a One-on-One Tutorial
  Get clear instructions, guidance and feedback from an expert to
  get your desired score.


                                                                       Use the
                                                             30-day study plan
                                                        in Show Time Package
 
TIPS FOR STUDYING IN 30 DAYS
                1. BUILD YOUR READING HABITS
                 Make sure you are exposing yourself to as much English language
                 content as you can, not just test-oriented readings: newspapers,
                 magazines- all help build reading speed.


                 2. BUILD YOUR LISTENING HABITS
                 Subscribe to podcasts, news channels on Youtube or watch
                 documentaries. Write down the words and ideas you hear. The
                 better your general listening ability is, the easier it is to hear the
                 words and follow the ideas.


        These should also give you vocabulary, and grammar, as well as
         ideas which will be really important in speaking and writing.



3. IMPROVE YOUR WRITING WITH FEEDBACK
Learn the task types and know the principles - what to do
and what not to do. Focus on clear ideas first. Then
practise and get feedback from a teacher. Review the
feedback to figure out what mistakes you’re making. Then
eliminate those mistakes.


4. IMPROVE SPEAKING WITH FEEDBACK
A teacher is incredibly important in helping you extend ideas,
improve grammar range/accuracy, pronunciation, and fluency.

EVEN A MONTH CAN MAKE A BIG DIFFERENCE!

                                                                  (Mini) Mock Test to get
                                                               writing/speaking feedback
 
ADVICE FROM JAY & MARK
                             JAY:
                             One thing we do in our live classes on E2Language.com is
                             we really go through the answers and the teacher explains
   UNDERSTAND                why B is correct, and then also why A and C and D are wrong.
  WHY AN ANSWER              So it's very clear.
   IS CORRECT/
    INCORRECT                It's a really good way to understand what's happening with
                             these tests because they are designed in a particular way,
                             and understanding why it is correct will help you answer
                             similar questions in the future.
                             MARK:
                             Understanding why the wrong answers were wrong is more
       The great news        important than getting them right.
        is, it will also
         make you a          Sometimes students get very excited about getting the
        better reader.       answers correct but we want you to focus more on why the
                             wrong answers were wrong so that in the future, you get
                             them right.



MARK:
You don't want to memorise anything. The questions that
you get on the test, you have no idea what they might be.              DON'T
So if you prepare one template, and then you deliver that           MEMORISE A
on your test, the examiner is going to look at that and              TEMPLATE
think, nope, they have not answered the question, and
that is going to very severely affect your score.

A lot of students will get into trouble because they go off
topic during the test and that can have a huge impact on
your score. So focus first on organising your writing so
your ideas are clear and then you get feedback on your
grammar.
